name: Fresh direct-thermal receipt paper
where_seen: Counter receipts and pick tickets torn from an 80 mm or 58 mm roll at a parts counter.
texture: Very smooth, plastic-like coated face with a faint satin sheen and almost no visible fibre; spec sheets give about 85-87% brightness, so it is a cool off-white rather than pure white (hex is an estimate).

name: Aged thermal paper, yellowed with faded print
where_seen: A receipt or ticket kept for a few years in a glovebox, wallet or file drawer.
texture: Coating turned yellow to brown, darker toward the edges, while the image loses contrast toward grey-brown; the sheet curls along its length (hexes are estimates).

name: Heat-darkened thermal paper
where_seen: A ticket left on a dashboard or under a hot cup, or scuffed by a fingernail, where the coating has developed on its own.
texture: Cloudy grey bloom and dark scuff streaks over the off-white face; stray heat and friction develop the leuco dye and obscure the print (hexes are estimates).
css: background: radial-gradient(circle at 70% 30%, rgba(40,36,38,.35), rgba(40,36,38,0) 45%), linear-gradient(100deg, rgba(40,36,38,0) 40%, rgba(40,36,38,.18) 41%, rgba(40,36,38,0) 43%), #CFCBC6;

name: End-of-roll stripe
where_seen: The last few feet of a receipt roll, where a coloured ink stripe warns the counter that the paper is nearly out.
texture: A translucent red or pink ink band, applied by an ink wheel along one or both edges or down the middle, on the last 3-6 feet of the roll; the print shows through it (hex is an estimate).

name: Thermal print with dead-dot streaks
where_seen: Tickets from a worn counter printer, where the same thin vertical white lines run through every line of print.
texture: One-dot-wide (0.125 mm at 203 dpi) unprinted vertical lines at fixed positions down the whole ticket, from failed or dirty print-head elements; overlay this on top of the text layer.
css: background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0 23%, #F7F6F1 23% calc(23% + 1px), transparent calc(23% + 1px) 61%, #F7F6F1 61% calc(61% + 2px), transparent calc(61% + 2px));

name: Inverse bar (white on black)
where_seen: The header or section band of a ticket, printed with the printer's white/black reverse mode.
texture: Solid thermal black, slightly uneven and soft-edged because it is built from 0.125 mm dots; large solids often print a shade lighter than text (unverified).

name: Blue-image thermal paper
where_seen: Older or budget rolls whose coating develops blue instead of black.
texture: Same smooth coated face as black-image paper; the image is a dull blue or blue-black from a different leuco dye family (hex is an estimate).
css: background: linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0,0,0,.03), rgba(0,0,0,0) 6%, rgba(0,0,0,0) 94%, rgba(0,0,0,.03)), #F6F5F0;

name: Yellow thermal paper
where_seen: Coloured rolls used to tell a shop copy or a pick ticket apart from the customer's white receipt.
texture: Tinted base stock with the same slick coated face; thermal papers are sold in brilliant white, beige and yellow (hex is an estimate).

name: Direct-thermal part tag stock
where_seen: A printed tag wired or stuck to a pulled part on a warehouse shelf, carrying stock number, vehicle, description and location.
texture: Heavier, flatter and brighter than receipt paper with a matte top coat; square die-cut corners and a barcode block (appearance and hexes unverified, tag contents sourced).
css: background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,.6), rgba(255,255,255,0) 30%), #FAFAF6; border: 1px solid #D9D6CC;

name: Faint print (low-density head or cheap roll)
where_seen: Tickets from a printer with a dirty head or a poorly coated roll, printing grey and patchy from the first day.
texture: Uneven, washed-out grey print with lighter patches across the width; poor coatings and dirty heads give faint, uneven images.
